Step 2: Evaluation of the Statements
Evaluating the assertion regarding sound speed in water compared to air: Sound speed in a fluid is given by \(v = \sqrt{ rac{B}{ ho}}\). Although water has a density \(\approx 1000\) times that of air, its bulk modulus \(B\) is roughly \(2 imes 10^4\) times greater than that of air. Consequently, the speed of sound in water (\(\approx 1482 ext{ m/s}\)) is substantially higher than in air (\(\approx 343 ext{ m/s}\)). Therefore, claiming that sound travels slower in water than in air is incorrect.
Evaluating the assertion regarding frequency and wavelength: Because frequency \( u\) remains unchanged across the boundary and the speed increases (\(v_{ ext{water}} > v_{ ext{air}}\)), the wavelength must increase in direct proportion (\(\lambda_{ ext{water}} > \lambda_{ ext{air}}\)). Therefore, asserting that frequency remains constant while wavelength increases is correct.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The proposition concerning frequency invariance and wavelength increase is correct, whereas the proposition asserting a lower sound speed in water is incorrect.

चरण 1: नियंत्रक सूत्र और सिद्धांत
तरंग की आवृत्ति \( u\) स्रोत के दोलनों द्वारा निर्धारित होती है और माध्यम बदलने पर अपरिवर्तित रहती है। तरंगदैर्घ्य, चाल और आवृत्ति में संबंध \(\lambda = rac{v}{ u}\) होता है।

चरण 2: कथनों का मूल्यांकन
जल में ध्वनि की चाल से संबंधित कथन का मूल्यांकन: किसी माध्यम में ध्वनि की चाल \(v = \sqrt{ rac{B}{ ho}}\) होती है। यद्यपि जल का घनत्व वायु से अधिक होता है, परंतु जल का आयतन प्रत्यास्थता गुणांक \(B\) वायु की तुलना में अत्यधिक बड़ा होता है। इस कारण जल में ध्वनि की चाल (\(\approx 1482 ext{ m/s}\)) वायु में चाल (\(\approx 343 ext{ m/s}\)) से काफी अधिक होती है। अतः जल में ध्वनि की चाल कम बताने वाला कथन गलत है।
आवृत्ति और तरंगदैर्घ्य से संबंधित कथन का मूल्यांकन: आवृत्ति \( u\) नियत रहती है तथा जल में प्रवेश करने पर चाल \(v\) बढ़ जाती है, अतः सूत्र \(\lambda = rac{v}{ u}\) के अनुसार जल में तरंगदैर्घ्य बढ़ जाती है। अतः यह कथन सत्य है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
आवृत्ति के अपरिवर्तित रहने तथा तरंगदैर्घ्य के बढ़ने से संबंधित कथन सही है, जबकि जल में ध्वनि की चाल कम बताने वाला कथन गलत है।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_STATEMENT_Q04 - Phase relationship and energy in standing waves

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In a standing wave formed on a stretched string, all constituent particles between any two successive nodes oscillate in the same phase.

Statement II: A standing wave continuously transports mechanical energy from one end of the string to the other.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: तनी हुई डोरी पर बनी अप्रगामी तरंग में किन्हीं दो क्रमागत निस्पंदों के बीच स्थित सभी कण समान कला में दोलन करते हैं।

कथन II: एक अप्रगामी तरंग डोरी के एक सिरे से दूसरे सिरे तक यांत्रिक ऊर्जा का निरंतर संचरण करती है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Governing Formulae and Principles
A stationary wave formed by the interference of two identical counter-propagating waves is described by \(y(x, t) = 2a \sin(kx) \cos(\omega t)\). The amplitude at any position \(x\) is given by \(\left|2a \sin(kx)\right|\), with nodes situated where \(\sin(kx) = 0\) (separated by \(\frac{\lambda}{2}\)).

Step 2: Evaluation of the Statements
Evaluating the assertion regarding particle phases: In the spatial interval between two consecutive nodes, the function \(\sin(kx)\) maintains a uniform algebraic sign. Consequently, every particle in that segment passes through its mean position simultaneously and achieves extreme displacement in the same direction at the same instant. Hence, all particles between two consecutive nodes vibrate in phase. This assertion is correct.
Evaluating the assertion regarding energy transport: Because nodes remain permanently stationary with zero displacement and zero velocity at all times, no mechanical work can be transferred across any nodal plane. Thus, mechanical energy remains confined between nodes as alternating kinetic and potential energy rather than propagating along the string. Hence, asserting continuous energy transport across the string is incorrect.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The proposition stating that particles between consecutive nodes oscillate in phase is correct, while the proposition asserting continuous longitudinal energy transport is incorrect.

चरण 1: नियंत्रक सूत्र और सिद्धांत
दो समान एवं विपरीत दिशाओं में गतिमान तरंगों के अध्यारोपण से बनी अप्रगामी तरंग का समीकरण \(y(x, t) = 2a \sin(kx) \cos(\omega t)\) होता है। किसी स्थिति \(x\) पर आयाम \(\left|2a \sin(kx)\right|\) होता है, तथा \(\sin(kx) = 0\) पर निस्पंद बनते हैं (जिनके बीच की दूरी \(\frac{\lambda}{2}\) होती है)।

चरण 2: कथनों का मूल्यांकन
कणों की कला से संबंधित कथन का मूल्यांकन: किन्हीं दो क्रमागत निस्पंदों के बीच \(\sin(kx)\) का बीजगणितीय चिह्न एकसमान रहता है। इसके कारण उस लूप के सभी कण एक साथ साम्यावस्था से गुजरते हैं तथा एक ही समय पर अपने अधिकतम विस्थापन पर पहुँचते हैं। अतः वे सभी समान कला में दोलन करते हैं। यह कथन सही है।
ऊर्जा संचरण से संबंधित कथन का मूल्यांकन: चूँकि निस्पंद सदैव स्थिर रहते हैं और उनका विस्थापन व वेग सदैव शून्य होता है, अतः निस्पंदों के आर-पार कोई कार्य या ऊर्जा स्थानांतरित नहीं हो सकती। ऊर्जा लूपों के बीच ही गतिज और स्थितिज ऊर्जा के रूप में परिबद्ध रहती है। अतः ऊर्जा के निरंतर आगे संचरण का कथन गलत है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
क्रमागत निस्पंदों के बीच कणों के समान कला में दोलन करने से संबंधित कथन सही है, जबकि डोरी में ऊर्जा के निरंतर संचरण से संबंधित कथन गलत है।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_STATEMENT_Q05 - Effect of pressure and temperature on sound

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: At a constant temperature, doubling the pressure of an ideal gas doubles the speed of sound in that gas.

Statement II: The speed of sound in an ideal gas is directly proportional to the square root of its absolute temperature.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: स्थिर ताप पर किसी आदर्श गैस का दाब दोगुना करने पर उसमें ध्वनि की चाल दोगुनी हो जाती है।

कथन II: किसी आदर्श गैस में ध्वनि की चाल उसके परम ताप के वर्गमूल के अनुक्रमानुपाती होती है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Governing Formula
According to Laplace's corrected formula, the speed of sound in an ideal gas is given by \(v = \sqrt{\frac{\gamma P}{\rho}} = \sqrt{\frac{\gamma R T}{M}}\), where \(\gamma\) is the adiabatic index, \(P\) is pressure, \(\rho\) is mass density, \(R\) is the universal gas constant, \(T\) is absolute temperature, and \(M\) is molar mass.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Statements
Evaluating the assertion regarding pressure variation at constant temperature: By Boyle's law at constant temperature, \(P \propto \rho\), which ensures that the ratio \(\frac{P}{\rho}\) remains completely invariant when pressure is changed. Therefore, changing or doubling the gas pressure produces no change in the speed of sound. Thus, the assertion that doubling pressure doubles sound speed is incorrect.
Evaluating the assertion regarding temperature dependence: From the expression \(v = \sqrt{\frac{\gamma R T}{M}}\), for a given gas with fixed \(\gamma\) and \(M\), the speed \(v\) is directly proportional to \(\sqrt{T}\). Hence, the assertion that speed is proportional to the square root of absolute temperature is correct.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The proposition concerning the doubling of sound speed with pressure is incorrect, whereas the proposition relating sound speed to the square root of absolute temperature is correct.

चरण 1: नियंत्रक सूत्र
लाप्लास के संशोधित सूत्र के अनुसार किसी आदर्श गैस में ध्वनि की चाल \(v = \sqrt{\frac{\gamma P}{\rho}} = \sqrt{\frac{\gamma R T}{M}}\) होती है, जहाँ \(\gamma\) रुद्धोष्म अनुपात, \(P\) दाब, \(\rho\) घनत्व, \(R\) सार्वत्रिक गैस नियतांक, \(T\) परम ताप और \(M\) मोलर द्रव्यमान है।

चरण 2: कथनों का मूल्यांकन
स्थिर ताप पर दाब परिवर्तन से संबंधित कथन का मूल्यांकन: बॉयल के नियमानुसार स्थिर ताप पर दाब बढ़ाने पर घनत्व भी उसी अनुपात में बढ़ता है (\(P \propto \rho\)), जिससे अनुपात \(\frac{P}{\rho}\) अपरिवर्तित रहता है। अतः स्थिर ताप पर दाब दोगुना करने से ध्वनि की चाल पर कोई प्रभाव नहीं पड़ता। इसलिए चाल दोगुनी होने वाला कथन गलत है।
तापमान निर्भरता से संबंधित कथन का मूल्यांकन: सूत्र \(v = \sqrt{\frac{\gamma R T}{M}}\) से स्पष्ट है कि नियत \(\gamma\) और \(M\) के लिए चाल \(v \propto \sqrt{T}\) होती है। अतः परम ताप के वर्गमूल के अनुक्रमानुपाती होने वाला कथन सही है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
दाब दोगुना करने पर ध्वनि की चाल दोगुनी होने से संबंधित कथन गलत है, जबकि चाल के परम ताप के वर्गमूल के अनुक्रमानुपाती होने से संबंधित कथन सही है।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_STATEMENT_Q06 - Harmonic frequencies in open and closed pipes

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: An organ pipe open at both ends produces both odd and even harmonics of its fundamental frequency.

Statement II: An organ pipe closed at one end produces only odd harmonics of its fundamental frequency.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: दोनों सिरों पर खुला आर्गन पाइप अपनी मूल आवृत्ति के विषम और सम दोनों संनादी उत्पन्न करता है।

कथन II: एक सिरे पर बंद आर्गन पाइप अपनी मूल आवृत्ति के केवल विषम संनादी ही उत्पन्न करता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Governing Formulae and Boundary Conditions
For standing longitudinal sound waves in an air column, an open end forms a displacement antinode, whereas a rigid closed end forms a displacement node.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Statements
Evaluating the assertion regarding an open pipe: A pipe of length \(L\) open at both ends has displacement antinodes at both ends, requiring \(L = n rac{\lambda}{2}\). The natural resonant frequencies are \( u_n = n\left( rac{v}{2L} ight) = n u_1\) where \(n = 1, 2, 3, 4, \ldots\). Thus, all integral multiples (both odd and even harmonics) are generated. This assertion is correct.
Evaluating the assertion regarding a closed pipe: A pipe of length \(L\) closed at one end has a displacement node at the closed end and an antinode at the open end, requiring \(L = (2m-1) rac{\lambda}{4}\). The resonant frequencies are \( u_m = (2m-1)\left( rac{v}{4L} ight) = (2m-1) u_1\) where \(m = 1, 2, 3, \ldots\). Thus, only odd multiples (odd harmonics) are present. This assertion is also correct.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both propositions describing the generation of harmonics in open and closed organ pipes are scientifically correct.

चरण 1: नियंत्रक सूत्र और परिसीमा स्थितियाँ
वायु स्तंभ में अनुदैर्ध्य अप्रगामी तरंगों के लिए, खुला सिरा विस्थापन प्रस्पंद बनाता है जबकि बंद सिरा विस्थापन निस्पंद बनाता है।

चरण 2: कथनों का मूल्यांकन
खुले आर्गन पाइप से संबंधित कथन का मूल्यांकन: दोनों सिरों पर खुले \(L\) लंबाई के पाइप के दोनों सिरों पर प्रस्पंद बनते हैं, जिससे \(L = n rac{\lambda}{2}\) प्राप्त होता है। इसकी अनुनादी आवृत्तियाँ \( u_n = n\left( rac{v}{2L} ight) = n u_1\) होती हैं जहाँ \(n = 1, 2, 3, 4, \dots\) है। अतः इसमें सभी सम एवं विषम संनादी उत्पन्न होते हैं। यह कथन सही है।
बंद आर्गन पाइप से संबंधित कथन का मूल्यांकन: एक सिरे पर बंद पाइप में बंद सिरे पर निस्पंद और खुले सिरे पर प्रस्पंद बनता है, जिससे \(L = (2m-1) rac{\lambda}{4}\) प्राप्त होता है। इसकी आवृत्तियाँ \( u_m = (2m-1)\left( rac{v}{4L} ight) = (2m-1) u_1\) होती हैं जहाँ \(m = 1, 2, 3, \dots\) है। अतः इसमें केवल विषम संनादी ही उपस्थित होते हैं। यह कथन भी सही है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
खुले तथा बंद आर्गन पाइपों में संनादी आवृत्तियों की उत्पत्ति से संबंधित दोनों कथन सही हैं।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_STATEMENT_Q07 - Boundary phase change and acoustic pressure nodes

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: When a mechanical wave reflects from a rigid fixed boundary, it suffers a phase reversal of \(\pi\) radians, whereas reflection at an open free boundary involves zero phase change.

Statement II: In a stationary longitudinal sound wave inside an air column, a displacement node corresponds to a position of minimum pressure variation (pressure node).

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: जब कोई यांत्रिक तरंग किसी दृढ़ स्थिर परिसीमा से परावर्तित होती है, तो उसमें \(\pi\) रेडियन का कला परिवर्तन होता है, जबकि मुक्त खुली परिसीमा से परावर्तन में शून्य कला परिवर्तन होता है।

कथन II: वायु स्तंभ के भीतर स्थिर अनुदैर्ध्य ध्वनि तरंग में, विस्थापन निस्पंद न्यूनतम दाब परिवर्तन की स्थिति (दाब निस्पंद) के संगत होता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Relevant Principles and Equations
Boundary conditions determine reflection characteristics: a fixed boundary enforces zero net displacement at all times, whereas a free end allows unrestrained motion. In longitudinal acoustic waves, acoustic pressure variation is related to displacement gradient by \(\Delta P = -B \frac{\partial s}{\partial x}\), where \(B\) is the bulk modulus.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Statements
Evaluating the assertion regarding boundary reflections: At a rigid fixed boundary, the boundary exerts an equal and opposite reaction force on the medium by Newton's third law, inverting the reflected pulse and introducing a phase shift of \(\pi\) radians (\(180^\circ\)). Conversely, at an unconstrained open boundary, the boundary moves freely without exerting an opposing force, returning the wave with zero phase change (\(\Delta \phi = 0\)). Thus, this assertion is correct.
Evaluating the assertion regarding displacement and pressure nodes: At a displacement node, particles remain stationary while particles on either side move toward or away from it with maximum relative displacement, making the spatial gradient \(\left|\frac{\partial s}{\partial x}\right|\) maximal. Consequently, the acoustic pressure fluctuation \(\left|\Delta P\right|\) reaches its maximum possible value, forming a pressure antinode (not a pressure node). Therefore, claiming that a displacement node corresponds to minimum pressure variation is incorrect.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The proposition concerning boundary reflection phase shifts is correct, whereas the proposition identifying a displacement node as a pressure node is incorrect.

चरण 1: संगत सिद्धांत और समीकरण
परिसीमा स्थितियाँ परावर्तन के व्यवहार को तय करती हैं: दृढ़ सिरा कुल विस्थापन को सदैव शून्य रखता है, जबकि मुक्त सिरा बिना किसी बाधा के गति करता है। अनुदैर्ध्य ध्वनि तरंगों में अतिरिक्त दाब परिवर्तन \(\Delta P = -B \frac{\partial s}{\partial x}\) द्वारा विस्थापन प्रवणता से संबंधित होता है।

चरण 2: कथनों का मूल्यांकन
परिसीमा परावर्तन से संबंधित कथन का मूल्यांकन: दृढ़ सिरे पर न्यूटन के तृतीय नियमानुसार विपरीत प्रतिक्रिया बल लगता है, जिससे परावर्तित तरंग उल्टी हो जाती है और उसमें \(\pi\) रेडियन (\(180^\circ\)) का कला परिवर्तन होता है। इसके विपरीत, मुक्त सिरे पर कोई विपरीत बल नहीं लगता, अतः परावर्तन बिना किसी कला परिवर्तन (\(0\) रेडियन) के होता है। अतः यह कथन सही है।
विस्थापन और दाब निस्पंद से संबंधित कथन का मूल्यांकन: विस्थापन निस्पंद पर कण स्थिर रहते हैं जबकि उसके दोनों ओर के कण अधिकतम सापेक्ष विस्थापन से गति करते हैं, जिससे विस्थापन प्रवणता \(\left|\frac{\partial s}{\partial x}\right|\) अधिकतम होती है। इसके फलस्वरूप दाब परिवर्तन \(\left|\Delta P\right|\) भी अधिकतम होता है, जो दाब प्रस्पंद बनाता है (दाब निस्पंद नहीं)। अतः विस्थापन निस्पंद को दाब निस्पंद बताने वाला कथन गलत है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
परिसीमा परावर्तन में कला परिवर्तन से संबंधित कथन सही है, जबकि विस्थापन निस्पंद को दाब निस्पंद बताने वाला कथन गलत है।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_STATEMENT_Q08 - Beat frequency generation and human auditory perception

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The phenomenon of acoustic beats arises from the superposition of two sound waves of identical frequencies propagating in opposite directions.

Statement II: When the difference in frequencies between two sounding bodies exceeds \(20\text{ Hz}\), the human ear easily perceives distinct periodic waxing and waning of sound intensity.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: ध्वनि विस्पंदों की परिघटना विपरीत दिशाओं में संचरित होने वाली समान आवृत्ति की दो ध्वनि तरंगों के अध्यारोपण से उत्पन्न होती है।

कथन II: जब दो ध्वनि स्रोतों की आवृत्तियों का अंतर \(20\text{ Hz}\) से अधिक हो जाता है, तो मानव कान ध्वनि की तीव्रता के आवर्ती उतार-चढ़ाव को आसानी से अलग-अलग सुन सकता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Relevant Principles and Formulae
Acoustic beats are temporal fluctuations in sound intensity resulting from the superposition of two waves of slightly different frequencies \( u_1\) and \( u_2\) travelling in the same direction, yielding a beat frequency \( u_{ ext{beat}} = \left| u_1 - u_2 ight|\). The human ear exhibits persistence of hearing of approximately \( rac{1}{10} ext{ s}\) (\(0.1 ext{ s}\)).

Step 2: Evaluation of the Statements
Evaluating the assertion concerning the generation of beats: Superposition of two identical waves travelling in opposite directions forms stationary (standing) waves, not beats. Beats strictly require two waves travelling along the same direction having slightly different frequencies. Hence, this assertion is incorrect.
Evaluating the assertion concerning human auditory detection of beats: Because the human auditory impression persists for roughly \(0.1 ext{ s}\), the brain cannot resolve distinct intensity peaks if they occur more rapidly than about \(10\) times per second. When the frequency difference exceeds \(10 ext{ to }20 ext{ Hz}\), the distinct periodic waxing and waning blend into a single continuous sensation of sound or a separate difference tone. Hence, asserting that the ear easily perceives distinct waxing and waning above \(20 ext{ Hz}\) is incorrect.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both propositions regarding the production of beats and the human auditory resolution of high beat frequencies are scientifically incorrect.

चरण 1: संगत सिद्धांत और सूत्र
विस्पंद एक ही दिशा में संचरित होने वाली थोड़ी भिन्न आवृत्तियों \( u_1\) और \( u_2\) की दो ध्वनि तरंगों के अध्यारोपण से उत्पन्न तीव्रता के आवर्ती उतार-चढ़ाव हैं, जिनकी विस्पंद आवृत्ति \( u_{ ext{beat}} = \left| u_1 - u_2 ight|\) होती है। मानव कान के लिए श्रवण निर्बंधता लगभग \( rac{1}{10}\) सेकंड (\(0.1 ext{ s}\)) होती है।

चरण 2: कथनों का मूल्यांकन
विस्पंदों की उत्पत्ति से संबंधित कथन का मूल्यांकन: विपरीत दिशाओं में चलने वाली समान आवृत्ति की दो तरंगों का अध्यारोपण अप्रगामी तरंगें उत्पन्न करता है, विस्पंद नहीं। विस्पंद के लिए तरंगों का एक ही दिशा में थोड़ी भिन्न आवृत्तियों के साथ संचरित होना आवश्यक है। अतः यह कथन गलत है।
मानव श्रवण द्वारा विस्पंद पहचान से संबंधित कथन का मूल्यांकन: श्रवण निर्बंधता (\(0.1 ext{ s}\)) के कारण यदि तीव्रता के उतार-चढ़ाव एक सेकंड में \(10\) बार से अधिक होते हैं, तो कान उन्हें अलग-अलग नहीं पहचान पाता। जब आवृत्ति अंतर \(10\) से \(20 ext{ Hz}\) से अधिक हो जाता है, तो उतार-चढ़ाव अलग सुनाई देने के बजाय एक निरंतर ध्वनि प्रभाव उत्पन्न करते हैं। अतः \(20 ext{ Hz}\) से अधिक पर विस्पंद स्पष्ट सुनाई देने का दावा गलत है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
विस्पंदों की उत्पत्ति तथा उच्च विस्पंद आवृत्ति पर श्रवण संवेदन से संबंधित दोनों कथन गलत हैं।

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_STATEMENT_Q01 - Classification and characteristics of mechanical waves

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements regarding wave motion:

Statement I: Mechanical waves require an elastic material medium for their propagation and cannot travel through vacuum.

Statement II: In a transverse mechanical wave, the constituent particles of the medium oscillate parallel to the direction of wave propagation.

Statement III: Sound waves in air are longitudinal waves that propagate through alternating compressions and rarefactions.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

तरंग गति के संबंध में नीचे तीन कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: यांत्रिक तरंगों के संचरण के लिए प्रत्यास्थ भौतिक माध्यम की आवश्यकता होती है और वे निर्वात में गमन नहीं कर सकती हैं।

कथन II: किसी अनुप्रस्थ यांत्रिक तरंग में माध्यम के घटक कण तरंग संचरण की दिशा के समांतर दोलन करते हैं।

कथन III: वायु में ध्वनि तरंगें अनुदैर्ध्य तरंगें होती हैं जो एकांतर संपीड़नों और विरलनों के माध्यम से संचरित होती हैं।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Mechanical waves transport energy through the elastic interaction and inertia of neighbouring particles in a material medium. Wave propagation is classified as transverse or longitudinal based on the direction of particle oscillations relative to the direction of energy propagation.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Statements
Evaluating the assertion regarding mechanical wave medium requirement: Mechanical waves (such as sound waves, seismic waves, or string vibrations) rely on mechanical restoring forces between particles and cannot propagate across vacuum. Hence, this assertion is scientifically valid.
Evaluating the assertion regarding transverse particle motion: By physical definition, particles in a transverse wave oscillate perpendicular (normal) to the direction of wave propagation, whereas parallel oscillations characterize longitudinal waves. Thus, claiming parallel oscillations in transverse waves is incorrect.
Evaluating the assertion regarding acoustic waves in air: Sound waves propagating in a gaseous medium consist of longitudinal compressions (regions of higher density and pressure) and rarefactions (regions of lower density and pressure). Hence, this assertion is scientifically valid.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The propositions regarding the medium requirement of mechanical waves and the longitudinal compression-rarefaction nature of sound in air are correct, whereas the proposition describing parallel particle motion in transverse waves is incorrect.

चरण 1: वैचारिक सिद्धांत
यांत्रिक तरंगें भौतिक माध्यम के घटक कणों की प्रत्यास्थता और जड़त्व के माध्यम से ऊर्जा का संचरण करती हैं। तरंग संचरण की दिशा के सापेक्ष कणों के दोलन की दिशा के आधार पर तरंगों को अनुप्रस्थ अथवा अनुदैर्ध्य में वर्गीकृत किया जाता है।

चरण 2: कथनों का मूल्यांकन
यांत्रिक तरंगों के लिए माध्यम की आवश्यकता से संबंधित कथन का मूल्यांकन: यांत्रिक तरंगों को आगे बढ़ने के लिए माध्यम के कणों के बीच प्रत्यानयन बलों की आवश्यकता होती है; वे निर्वात में संचरित नहीं हो सकती हैं। अतः यह कथन सही है।
अनुप्रस्थ तरंगों में कण गति से संबंधित कथन का मूल्यांकन: अनुप्रस्थ तरंगों में माध्यम के कण तरंग संचरण की दिशा के लंबवत दोलन करते हैं, जबकि समांतर दोलन अनुदैर्ध्य तरंगों का लक्षण है। अतः अनुप्रस्थ तरंगों में समांतर दोलन बताने वाला कथन गलत है।
वायु में ध्वनि तरंगों से संबंधित कथन का मूल्यांकन: वायु में ध्वनि तरंगें एकांतर संपीड़न (उच्च घनत्व व दाब का क्षेत्र) और विरलन (निम्न घनत्व व दाब का क्षेत्र) के रूप में चलने वाली अनुदैर्ध्य तरंगें होती हैं। अतः यह कथन सही है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
यांत्रिक तरंगों हेतु माध्यम की अनिवार्यता तथा वायु में ध्वनि के अनुदैर्ध्य स्वरूप से संबंधित कथन सही हैं, जबकि अनुप्रस्थ तरंगों में समांतर कण गति से संबंधित कथन गलत है।

answer.text: Statements I and III only are correct.
Statements I and II only are correct.
Statements II and III only are correct.
Statements I, II and III are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_STATEMENT_Q02 - Speed of waves in different media

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements regarding wave motion:

Statement I: The speed of a transverse wave on a stretched string is directly proportional to the square root of the tension in the string.

Statement II: The speed of sound in an ideal gas at constant temperature increases significantly when the pressure of the gas is doubled.

Statement III: The speed of sound in liquids and solids is generally much higher than in gases because their elastic moduli are several orders of magnitude greater.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

तरंग गति के संबंध में नीचे तीन कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: तनी हुई डोरी पर अनुप्रस्थ तरंग की चाल डोरी में तनाव के वर्गमूल के अनुक्रमानुपाती होती है।

कथन II: स्थिर ताप पर किसी आदर्श गैस का दाब दोगुना करने पर उसमें ध्वनि की चाल में उल्लेखनीय वृद्धि होती है।

कथन III: द्रवों और ठोसों में ध्वनि की चाल सामान्यतः गैसों की तुलना में काफी अधिक होती है क्योंकि उनके प्रत्यास्थता गुणांक कई गुना अधिक होते हैं।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Governing Formulae and Principles
The speed of transverse waves on a stretched string is \(v = \sqrt{\frac{T}{\mu}}\), where \(T\) is tension and \(\mu\) is linear mass density. The speed of longitudinal sound waves in a general medium is \(v = \sqrt{\frac{E}{\rho}}\), and for an ideal gas with Laplace's correction it is \(v = \sqrt{\frac{\gamma P}{\rho}} = \sqrt{\frac{\gamma R T}{M}}\).

Step 2: Evaluation of the Statements
Evaluating the assertion regarding wave speed on a stretched string: From \(v = \sqrt{\frac{T}{\mu}}\), for a given string of fixed linear mass density, wave speed is directly proportional to \(\sqrt{T}\). Hence, this assertion is correct.
Evaluating the assertion regarding sound speed dependence on gas pressure: At isothermal conditions (constant \(T\)), according to Boyle's law, doubling the pressure \(P\) causes an identical doubling in density \(\rho\), keeping the ratio \(\frac{P}{\rho}\) constant. Therefore, the speed of sound remains independent of pressure at constant temperature. Hence, asserting that speed increases significantly with pressure is incorrect.
Evaluating the assertion regarding sound speeds in condensed media versus gases: Although solids and liquids possess significantly greater densities than gases, their bulk and Young's moduli are \(10^4\) to \(10^5\) times larger due to strong intermolecular binding forces. Consequently, the ratio \(\frac{E}{\rho}\) is much higher, resulting in faster propagation speeds. Hence, this assertion is correct.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The propositions relating string wave speed to the square root of tension and explaining higher acoustic speeds in condensed media are correct, whereas the proposition claiming sound speed changes with pressure at constant temperature is incorrect.

चरण 1: नियंत्रक सूत्र और सिद्धांत
तनी हुई डोरी पर अनुप्रस्थ तरंग की चाल \(v = \sqrt{\frac{T}{\mu}}\) होती है, जहाँ \(T\) तनाव तथा \(\mu\) रेखीय द्रव्यमान घनत्व है। किसी माध्यम में ध्वनि तरंगों की चाल \(v = \sqrt{\frac{E}{\rho}}\) होती है, तथा आदर्श गैस में लाप्लास संशोधन के साथ \(v = \sqrt{\frac{\gamma P}{\rho}} = \sqrt{\frac{\gamma R T}{M}}\) होती है।

चरण 2: कथनों का मूल्यांकन
डोरी पर तरंग की चाल से संबंधित कथन का मूल्यांकन: सूत्र \(v = \sqrt{\frac{T}{\mu}}\) के अनुसार नियत \(\mu\) के लिए चाल \(v \propto \sqrt{T}\) होती है। अतः तनाव के वर्गमूल के अनुक्रमानुपाती होने का कथन सही है।
गैस में दाब निर्भरता से संबंधित कथन का मूल्यांकन: स्थिर ताप पर बॉयल के नियमानुसार दाब बढ़ाने पर घनत्व भी उसी अनुपात में बढ़ता है, जिससे अनुपात \(\frac{P}{\rho}\) नियत रहता है। अतः स्थिर ताप पर दाब बदलने से चाल नहीं बदलती। इसलिए चाल में उल्लेखनीय वृद्धि का दावा गलत है।
ठोसों और द्रवों में ध्वनि की चाल से संबंधित कथन का मूल्यांकन: यद्यपि ठोसों और द्रवों का घनत्व अधिक होता है, परंतु उनके प्रत्यास्थता गुणांक गैसों की तुलना में अत्यधिक बड़े होते हैं। इसके कारण अनुपात \(\frac{E}{\rho}\) अधिक होता है और ध्वनि तेजी से चलती है। अतः यह कथन सही है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
डोरी में तनाव निर्भरता तथा सघन माध्यमों में ध्वनि की अधिक चाल से संबंधित कथन सही हैं, जबकि स्थिर ताप पर दाब के साथ चाल में वृद्धि बताने वाला कथन गलत है।

answer.text: Statements I and II only are correct.
Statements I and III only are correct.
Statements II and III only are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_STATEMENT_Q03 - Standing wave characteristics in air columns

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements regarding wave motion:

Statement I: In a stationary longitudinal sound wave in an air column, a displacement node corresponds to a pressure antinode.

Statement II: An organ pipe closed at one end produces only odd harmonics of its fundamental frequency.

Statement III: An organ pipe open at both ends produces both odd and even harmonics of its fundamental frequency.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

तरंग गति के संबंध में नीचे तीन कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: वायु स्तंभ में स्थिर अनुदैर्ध्य ध्वनि तरंग में, विस्थापन निस्पंद दाब प्रस्पंद के संगत होता है।

कथन II: एक सिरे पर बंद आर्गन पाइप अपनी मूल आवृत्ति के केवल विषम संनादी ही उत्पन्न करता है।

कथन III: दोनों सिरों पर खुला आर्गन पाइप अपनी मूल आवृत्ति के विषम और सम दोनों संनादी उत्पन्न करता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Relevant Equations and Boundary Conditions
In longitudinal waves, acoustic excess pressure is proportional to the spatial derivative of displacement: \(\Delta P = -B rac{\partial s}{\partial x}\). For pipes, open ends enforce displacement antinodes (pressure nodes), while closed ends enforce displacement nodes (pressure antinodes).

Step 2: Evaluation of the Statements
Evaluating the assertion regarding displacement and pressure extrema: At positions where displacement is zero (displacement nodes), particles on either side undergo opposite movements, producing the largest compression or rarefaction (maximum spatial gradient \(\left| rac{\partial s}{\partial x} ight|\)). Hence, pressure variations are maximal at displacement nodes, making them pressure antinodes. This assertion is correct.
Evaluating the assertion regarding a closed organ pipe: An air column of length \(L\) closed at one end has a displacement node at the closed end and an antinode at the open end, giving resonant modes \(L = (2m-1) rac{\lambda}{4}\) and frequencies \( u_m = (2m-1) rac{v}{4L}\) for \(m = 1, 2, 3, \ldots\). Thus, only odd harmonics are generated. This assertion is correct.
Evaluating the assertion regarding an open organ pipe: An air column of length \(L\) open at both ends has displacement antinodes at both boundaries, giving resonant modes \(L = n rac{\lambda}{2}\) and frequencies \( u_n = n rac{v}{2L}\) for \(n = 1, 2, 3, \ldots\). Thus, all integral multiples (both odd and even harmonics) are present. This assertion is also correct.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
All three propositions regarding acoustic pressure nodes and the harmonic spectrum of closed and open pipes are scientifically correct.

चरण 1: संगत समीकरण और परिसीमा स्थितियाँ
अनुदैर्ध्य तरंगों में अतिरिक्त दाब \(\Delta P = -B rac{\partial s}{\partial x}\) होता है। पाइपों में खुले सिरे विस्थापन प्रस्पंद (दाब निस्पंद) बनाते हैं तथा बंद सिरे विस्थापन निस्पंद (दाब प्रस्पंद) बनाते हैं।

चरण 2: कथनों का मूल्यांकन
विस्थापन और दाब चरम मानों से संबंधित कथन का मूल्यांकन: जहाँ विस्थापन शून्य होता है (विस्थापन निस्पंद), वहाँ विस्थापन में दूरी के साथ परिवर्तन की दर \(\left| rac{\partial s}{\partial x} ight|\) अधिकतम होती है, जिससे संपीड़न या विरलन अधिकतम होता है। अतः विस्थापन निस्पंद पर दाब परिवर्तन अधिकतम होता है (दाब प्रस्पंद)। यह कथन सही है।
बंद आर्गन पाइप से संबंधित कथन का मूल्यांकन: एक सिरे पर बंद पाइप में बंद सिरे पर निस्पंद तथा खुले सिरे पर प्रस्पंद बनता है, जिससे अनुनादी आवृत्तियाँ \( u_m = (2m-1) rac{v}{4L}\) प्राप्त होती हैं। अतः इसमें केवल विषम संनादी ही उत्पन्न होते हैं। यह कथन सही है।
खुले आर्गन पाइप से संबंधित कथन का मूल्यांकन: दोनों सिरों पर खुले पाइप में दोनों सिरों पर प्रस्पंद बनते हैं, जिससे अनुनादी आवृत्तियाँ \( u_n = n rac{v}{2L}\) होती हैं। अतः इसमें सभी सम एवं विषम संनादी उपस्थित होते हैं। यह कथन भी सही है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
विस्थापन निस्पंद के दाब प्रस्पंद होने तथा बंद व खुले पाइपों के संनादी वर्णक्रम से संबंधित तीनों कथन सही हैं।

answer.text: Statements I and II only are correct.
Statements II and III only are correct.
Statements I, II and III are correct.
Statements I and III only are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_STATEMENT_Q04 - Wave interference reflection and beat phenomena

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements regarding wave motion:

Statement I: When two harmonic waves of equal amplitude and equal frequency travelling in the same direction interfere destructively with a phase difference of \(\pi\) radians, the resultant displacement is zero everywhere at all times.

Statement II: When a transverse wave on a string reflects from a free boundary, the reflected wave undergoes a phase reversal of \(\pi\) radians.

Statement III: When two sound sources with frequencies differing by more than \(20\text{ Hz}\) are sounded together, the human ear easily perceives distinct individual waxing and waning beats due to the persistence of hearing.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

तरंग गति के संबंध में नीचे तीन कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: जब समान आयाम और समान आवृत्ति की दो प्रगामी तरंगें एक ही दिशा में \(\pi\) रेडियन के कलांतर के साथ विनाशी व्यतिकरण करती हैं, तो परिणामी विस्थापन प्रत्येक स्थान पर सदैव शून्य होता है।

कथन II: जब डोरी पर अनुप्रस्थ तरंग किसी मुक्त परिसीमा से परावर्तित होती है, तो परावर्तित तरंग में \(\pi\) रेडियन का कला परिवर्तन होता है।

कथन III: जब \(20\text{ Hz}\) से अधिक आवृत्ति अंतर वाले दो ध्वनि स्रोत एक साथ बजाए जाते हैं, तो श्रवण निर्बंधता के कारण मानव कान अलग-अलग विस्पंदों के उतार-चढ़ाव को आसानी से स्पष्ट सुन सकता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Relevant Mathematical Principles
The superposition of two identical waves with phase difference \(\phi\) gives a resultant amplitude of \(A(\phi) = 2a \cos\left(\frac{\phi}{2}\right)\). Boundary reflections follow dynamic constraints based on boundary rigidity. Beat perception depends on auditory persistence (\(\approx 0.1\text{ s}\)).

Step 2: Evaluation of the Statements
Evaluating the assertion regarding destructive interference: For two identical harmonic waves co-propagating with phase difference \(\phi = \pi\), the resultant amplitude is \(A(\pi) = 2a \cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) = 0\). The displacements of the two waves cancel each other completely at every coordinate \(x\) and time \(t\), yielding \(y(x,t) = 0\) everywhere at all times. Hence, this assertion is correct.
Evaluating the assertion regarding reflection at a free boundary: At an unconstrained free boundary (such as a ring sliding without friction on a rod), the boundary moves freely with the disturbance, so the reflected wave returns with zero phase shift (\(\Delta \phi = 0\)). A phase reversal of \(\pi\) radians occurs only upon reflection at a rigid fixed boundary. Hence, this assertion is incorrect.
Evaluating the assertion regarding beat perception: Due to the persistence of hearing of roughly \(0.1\text{ s}\), the human ear can resolve periodic waxing and waning only when the beat frequency does not exceed about \(10\text{ Hz}\). When the frequency difference exceeds \(20\text{ Hz}\), the intensity fluctuations succeed each other too rapidly to be perceived as individual beats, blending instead into a continuous sound. Hence, this assertion is incorrect.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The proposition concerning total cancellation in destructive interference is correct, whereas the propositions regarding phase reversal at a free boundary and auditory resolution of high-frequency beats are incorrect.

चरण 1: संगत गणितीय सिद्धांत
समान तरंगों के अध्यारोपण में परिणामी आयाम \(A(\phi) = 2a \cos\left(\frac{\phi}{2}\right)\) होता है। परिसीमा से परावर्तन परिसीमा की दृढ़ता पर निर्भर करता है। विस्पंदों की पहचान मानव श्रवण निर्बंधता (लगभग \(0.1\text{ s}\)) द्वारा सीमित होती है।

चरण 2: कथनों का मूल्यांकन
विनाशी व्यतिकरण से संबंधित कथन का मूल्यांकन: एक ही दिशा में गतिमान समान तरंगों में यदि कलांतर \(\phi = \pi\) हो, तो परिणामी आयाम \(A(\pi) = 2a \cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) = 0\) हो जाता है। तरंगें प्रत्येक बिंदु और प्रत्येक क्षण एक-दूसरे को पूर्णतः निरस्त कर देती हैं, जिससे परिणामी विस्थापन सर्वत्र शून्य रहता है। अतः यह कथन सही है।
मुक्त परिसीमा से परावर्तन से संबंधित कथन का मूल्यांकन: मुक्त परिसीमा (जैसे छड़ पर घर्षणहीन छल्ला) पर कोई विपरीत बल नहीं लगता, अतः परावर्तित तरंग बिना किसी कला परिवर्तन (\(0\) रेडियन) के लौटती है। \(\pi\) रेडियन का कला परिवर्तन केवल दृढ़ परिसीमा से परावर्तन पर होता है। अतः यह कथन गलत है।
विस्पंद श्रवण संवेदन से संबंधित कथन का मूल्यांकन: लगभग \(0.1\) सेकंड की श्रवण निर्बंधता के कारण मानव कान केवल तभी अलग-अलग विस्पंद पहचान सकता है जब आवृत्ति अंतर लगभग \(10\text{ Hz}\) से कम हो। \(20\text{ Hz}\) से अधिक होने पर उतार-चढ़ाव इतनी तेजी से होते हैं कि वे अलग-अलग सुनाई देने के बजाय एक निरंतर ध्वनि में मिल जाते हैं। अतः यह कथन गलत है।

चरण 3: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
विनाशी व्यतिकरण में कुल विस्थापन शून्य होने से संबंधित कथन सही है, जबकि मुक्त परिसीमा पर कला परिवर्तन तथा उच्च आवृत्ति पर विस्पंदों के स्पष्ट सुनाई देने से संबंधित कथन गलत हैं।

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_MATCH_Q01 - Wave propagation speeds across different physical media

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I List-II
A. Transverse wave on a stretched stringI. \(\sqrt{\frac{Y}{\rho}}\)
B. Longitudinal wave in a fluid (bulk modulus \(B\))II. \(\sqrt{\frac{T}{\mu}}\)
C. Longitudinal wave in an ideal gas (Laplace corrected)III. \(\sqrt{\frac{\gamma P}{\rho}}\)
D. Longitudinal wave in a solid rod (Young's modulus \(Y\))IV. \(\sqrt{\frac{B}{\rho}}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Wave speed on a stretched string
For a stretched string under tension \(T\) and having linear mass density \(\mu\), the restoring force is supplied by tension and the inertial parameter is \(\mu\). The transverse wave speed is given by \(v = \sqrt{\frac{T}{\mu}}\). Thus, transverse wave on a stretched string corresponds to \(\sqrt{\frac{T}{\mu}}\).

Step 2: Longitudinal wave speed in a fluid
In a fluid medium of bulk modulus \(B\) and mass density \(\rho\), compressions and rarefactions depend on the volume elasticity. The speed of a longitudinal wave is given by \(v = \sqrt{\frac{B}{\rho}}\). Thus, longitudinal wave in a fluid corresponds to \(\sqrt{\frac{B}{\rho}}\).

Step 3: Laplace-corrected sound speed in an ideal gas
For an ideal gas, acoustic oscillations occur adiabatically with adiabatic bulk modulus \(B_{\text{ad}} = \gamma P\). The speed of sound is given by the Laplace formula \(v = \sqrt{\frac{\gamma P}{\rho}}\). Thus, longitudinal wave in an ideal gas corresponds to \(\sqrt{\frac{\gamma P}{\rho}}\).

Step 4: Longitudinal wave speed in a solid rod
In a slender solid bar or rod of Young's modulus \(Y\) and density \(\rho\), longitudinal strain dominates with negligible lateral restraint. The speed of longitudinal waves is given by \(v = \sqrt{\frac{Y}{\rho}}\). Thus, longitudinal wave in a solid rod corresponds to \(\sqrt{\frac{Y}{\rho}}\).

Step 5: Synthesis and Final Conclusion
Combining all four evaluated relationships yields the complete set of correspondences: A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I.

Final Answer
A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_MATCH_Q02 - Physical quantities and fundamental wave relations

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I List-II
A. Angular wave number (\(k\))I. \(|\nu_1 - \nu_2|\)
B. Angular frequency (\(\omega\))II. \(2a \cos\left(\frac{\phi}{2}\right)\)
C. Beat frequency (\(\nu_{\text{beat}}\))III. \(\frac{2\pi}{\lambda}\)
D. Resultant amplitude in wave interference (\(A\))IV. \(\frac{2\pi}{T}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Angular wave number
The angular wave number (or propagation constant) represents the spatial frequency of the wave and is defined as \(k = \frac{2\pi}{\lambda}\), where \(\lambda\) is the wavelength. Thus, angular wave number corresponds to \(\frac{2\pi}{\lambda}\).

Step 2: Angular frequency
The angular frequency represents the temporal rate of change of phase and is related to the time period \(T\) by \(\omega = \frac{2\pi}{T} = 2\pi \nu\). Thus, angular frequency corresponds to \(\frac{2\pi}{T}\).

Step 3: Beat frequency
When two harmonic sound waves of slightly different frequencies \(\nu_1\) and \(\nu_2\) interfere, the waxing and waning of acoustic intensity occurs at a frequency equal to the absolute difference \(\nu_{\text{beat}} = |\nu_1 - \nu_2|\). Thus, beat frequency corresponds to \(|\nu_1 - \nu_2|\).

Step 4: Resultant interference amplitude
When two identical sinusoidal waves of amplitude \(a\) interfere with a phase difference \(\phi\), trigonometric superposition yields a resultant wave amplitude of \(A = 2a \cos\left(\frac{\phi}{2}\right)\). Thus, resultant amplitude corresponds to \(2a \cos\left(\frac{\phi}{2}\right)\).

Step 5: Synthesis and Final Conclusion
Combining all four evaluated relationships yields the complete set of correspondences: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

Final Answer
A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_MATCH_Q03 - Boundary reflection characteristics and stationary wave nodes

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I List-II
A. Reflection of a wave pulse from a rigid fixed boundaryI. Zero phase shift with maximum boundary displacement \(2a\)
B. Reflection of a wave pulse from an open free boundaryII. Phase reversal of \(\pi\) radians with zero boundary displacement
C. Position of nodes on a string fixed at both endsIII. \(\left(n + \frac{1}{2}\right)\frac{\lambda}{2}\) where \(n = 0, 1, 2, \dots\)
D. Position of antinodes on a string fixed at both endsIV. \(\frac{n\lambda}{2}\) where \(n = 0, 1, 2, \dots\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Reflection at a rigid fixed boundary
At a rigid boundary, the string end is constrained to zero displacement (\(y = 0\)). The support exerts a reactive force producing an inverted reflected pulse. This produces a phase change of \(\pi\text{ radians}\) with permanent zero displacement at the boundary. Thus, reflection from a rigid fixed boundary corresponds to phase reversal of \(\pi\) radians with zero boundary displacement.

Step 2: Reflection at an open free boundary
At a completely free boundary, the end point is unrestricted and cannot support transverse force (\(\frac{\partial y}{\partial x} = 0\)). The incident and reflected waves interfere constructively in phase (zero phase shift), creating a maximum displacement equal to twice the pulse amplitude (\(2a\)). Thus, reflection from an open free boundary corresponds to zero phase shift with maximum boundary displacement \(2a\).

Step 3: Positions of nodes on a fixed string
In the stationary wave \(y = 2a \sin(kx) \cos(\omega t)\) with boundary condition \(y(0) = 0\), nodes occur where \(\sin(kx) = 0\), yielding \(kx = n\pi\) or \(x = \frac{n\lambda}{2}\) for \(n = 0, 1, 2, \dots\). Thus, position of nodes corresponds to \(\frac{n\lambda}{2}\).

Step 4: Positions of antinodes on a fixed string
Antinodes occur where the amplitude \(|\sin(kx)| = 1\), yielding \(kx = \left(n + \frac{1}{2}\right)\pi\) or \(x = \left(n + \frac{1}{2}\right)\frac{\lambda}{2}\) for \(n = 0, 1, 2, \dots\). Thus, position of antinodes corresponds to \(\left(n + \frac{1}{2}\right)\frac{\lambda}{2}\).

Step 5: Synthesis and Final Conclusion
Combining all four evaluated relationships yields the complete set of correspondences: A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

Final Answer
A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_MATCH_Q04 - Resonant harmonic frequencies in strings and acoustic pipes

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I List-II
A. Fundamental mode of a string of length \(L\) fixed at both endsI. \(\frac{v}{L}\)
B. Fundamental mode of an organ pipe of length \(L\) closed at one endII. \(\frac{3v}{4L}\)
C. Second harmonic of an organ pipe of length \(L\) open at both endsIII. \(\frac{v}{2L}\)
D. Third harmonic of an organ pipe of length \(L\) closed at one endIV. \(\frac{v}{4L}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Fundamental mode of a string fixed at both ends
For a string of length \(L\) clamped at both ends, the fundamental mode corresponds to a single loop with \(L = \frac{\lambda}{2}\), giving wavelength \(\lambda = 2L\). The fundamental frequency is \(\nu_1 = \frac{v}{\lambda} = \frac{v}{2L}\). Thus, fundamental mode of a string fixed at both ends corresponds to \(\frac{v}{2L}\).

Step 2: Fundamental mode of an organ pipe closed at one end
An organ pipe of length \(L\) closed at one end has a displacement node at the closed end and an antinode at the open end. In the fundamental mode, \(L = \frac{\lambda}{4}\), giving \(\lambda = 4L\). The fundamental frequency is \(\nu_1 = \frac{v}{4L}\). Thus, fundamental mode of an organ pipe closed at one end corresponds to \(\frac{v}{4L}\).

Step 3: Second harmonic of an organ pipe open at both ends
An open organ pipe forms antinodes at both ends. Its harmonic frequencies are given by \(\nu_n = \frac{nv}{2L}\) for \(n = 1, 2, 3, \dots\). For the second harmonic (\(n = 2\)), the frequency is \(\nu_2 = 2\left(\frac{v}{2L}\right) = \frac{v}{L}\). Thus, second harmonic of an organ pipe open at both ends corresponds to \(\frac{v}{L}\).

Step 4: Third harmonic of an organ pipe closed at one end
An organ pipe closed at one end produces only odd harmonics, given by \(\nu_n = (2n - 1)\frac{v}{4L}\). The fundamental mode (\(n = 1\)) is \(\frac{v}{4L}\), and the next higher mode is the third harmonic, which is three times the fundamental frequency: \(\nu_3 = 3\left(\frac{v}{4L}\right) = \frac{3v}{4L}\). Thus, third harmonic of an organ pipe closed at one end corresponds to \(\frac{3v}{4L}\).

Step 5: Synthesis and Final Conclusion
Combining all four evaluated relationships yields the complete set of correspondences: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

Final Answer
A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_NUMERICAL_Q01 - Wavelength calculation of radio wave from frequency

questiontext.text: A radio station broadcasts an electromagnetic signal at a frequency of \(600\text{ kHz}\). Given that the speed of light in vacuum is \(c = 3.0 \times 10^8\text{ m s}^{-1}\), what is the wavelength of the transmitted electromagnetic wave?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1:
Identify the given values: speed \(c = 3.0 imes 10^8 ext{ m s}^{-1}\) and frequency \( u = 600 ext{ kHz} = 6.0 imes 10^5 ext{ Hz}\).

Step 2:
Recall the fundamental wave relation connecting wave speed, frequency, and wavelength: \[c = u \lambda\]

Step 3:
Rearrange the equation to solve for wavelength \(\lambda\): \[\lambda = rac{c}{ u}\]

Step 4:
Substitute the values into the formula: \[\lambda = rac{3.0 imes 10^8 ext{ m s}^{-1}}{6.0 imes 10^5 ext{ s}^{-1}} = 500 ext{ m}\]

Final Answer:
The wavelength of the transmitted radio wave is \(500 ext{ m}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_NUMERICAL_Q02 - Determination of wavelength and frequency from wave equation

questiontext.text: A travelling transverse wave is described by \(y(x, t) = 0.04 \sin(15.7 x - 314 t)\), where \(x\) and \(y\) are in metres and \(t\) is in seconds. Taking \(\pi \approx 3.14\), what are the wavelength \(\lambda\) and frequency \(\nu\) of this wave?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1:
Compare the given wave equation \(y(x, t) = 0.04 \sin(15.7 x - 314 t)\) with the standard harmonic equation \(y(x, t) = a \sin(kx - \omega t)\).

Step 2:
Identify the angular wave number \(k = 15.7\text{ rad m}^{-1}\) and angular frequency \(\omega = 314\text{ rad s}^{-1}\).

Step 3:
Calculate the wavelength using \(\lambda = \frac{2\pi}{k}\): \[\lambda = \frac{2 \times 3.14}{15.7} = \frac{6.28}{15.7} = 0.40\text{ m}\]

Step 4:
Calculate the frequency using \(\nu = \frac{\omega}{2\pi}\): \[\nu = \frac{314}{2 \times 3.14} = 50\text{ Hz}\]

Final Answer:
The wavelength is \(0.40\text{ m}\) and the frequency is \(50\text{ Hz}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_NUMERICAL_Q03 - Displacement calculation at given position and time

questiontext.text: A travelling wave along a string is given by \(y(x, t) = 0.005 \sin(80.0 x - 3.0 t)\), where all numerical constants are in SI units. What is the displacement \(y\) of the string element at \(x = 0.30\text{ m}\) at time \(t = 20.0\text{ s}\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1:
Substitute \(x = 0.30\text{ m}\) and \(t = 20.0\text{ s}\) into the argument of the sine function: \[\theta = 80.0(0.30) - 3.0(20.0) = 24.0 - 60.0 = -36.0\text{ rad}\]

Step 2:
Reduce the angle modulo \(2\pi\) to find the principal angle: \[\theta' = -36.0 + 12\pi = -36.0 + 12(3.14159) = -36.0 + 37.699 = 1.699\text{ rad}\]

Step 3:
Convert radians to degrees: \(1.699 \times \frac{180^{\circ}}{\pi} \approx 97.35^{\circ}\).

Step 4:
Evaluate \(\sin(1.699\text{ rad}) = \sin(97.35^{\circ}) \approx 0.9918 \approx 1.0\).

Step 5:
Calculate displacement: \[y = 0.005\text{ m} \times 0.9918 \approx 5.0\text{ mm}\]

Final Answer:
The displacement of the element is approximately \(5.0\text{ mm}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_NUMERICAL_Q04 - Maximum particle speed and maximum acceleration calculation

questiontext.text: A sinusoidal wave travelling on a stretched string has an amplitude of \(2.0\text{ cm}\) and a frequency of \(25.0\text{ Hz}\). Taking \(\pi \approx 3.14\), what are the maximum transverse particle speed and maximum transverse particle acceleration of any element of the string?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1:
List the given values in SI units: amplitude \(a = 2.0\text{ cm} = 0.020\text{ m}\), frequency \(\nu = 25.0\text{ Hz}\).

Step 2:
Calculate the angular frequency: \[\omega = 2\pi \nu = 2 \times 3.1416 \times 25.0 = 50\pi\text{ rad s}^{-1} \approx 157.1\text{ rad s}^{-1}\]

Step 3:
Calculate the maximum transverse particle speed: \[v_{p,\text{max}} = \omega a = (50\pi\text{ s}^{-1}) \times (0.020\text{ m}) = \pi\text{ m s}^{-1} \approx 3.14\text{ m s}^{-1}\]

Step 4:
Calculate the maximum transverse particle acceleration: \[a_{p,\text{max}} = \omega^2 a = (157.08\text{ s}^{-1})^2 \times (0.020\text{ m}) = 24674 \times 0.020 \approx 493.5\text{ m s}^{-2} \approx 493\text{ m s}^{-2}\]

Final Answer:
The maximum speed is \(3.14\text{ m s}^{-1}\) and the maximum acceleration is \(493\text{ m s}^{-2}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_NUMERICAL_Q05 - Wavelength calculation when maximum particle speed equals four wave speeds

questiontext.text: A progressive harmonic wave of amplitude \(a = 5.0\text{ cm}\) propagates along a string. If the maximum transverse speed of the string particles is four times the wave propagation speed, what is the wavelength \(\lambda\) of the wave?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1:
Write the formula for maximum transverse particle speed: \(v_{p,\text{max}} = \omega a\).

Step 2:
Write the formula for wave propagation speed: \(v = \frac{\omega}{k}\).

Step 3:
Apply the given condition \(v_{p,\text{max}} = 4 v\): \[\omega a = 4 \left(\frac{\omega}{k}\right) \implies a = \frac{4}{k}\]

Step 4:
Express the wave number in terms of wavelength: \(k = \frac{2\pi}{\lambda}\).

Step 5:
Substitute \(k\) into the relation: \[a = \frac{4}{\frac{2\pi}{\lambda}} = \frac{2\lambda}{\pi} \implies \lambda = \frac{\pi a}{2}\]

Step 6:
Substitute \(a = 5.0\text{ cm} = 0.050\text{ m}\): \[\lambda = \frac{\pi \times 5.0\text{ cm}}{2} = 2.5\pi\text{ cm} \approx 7.85\text{ cm} = 0.0785\text{ m}\]

Final Answer:
The wavelength is \(7.85\text{ cm}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_NUMERICAL_Q06 - Phase difference calculation for points four metres apart

questiontext.text: A travelling wave is described by \(y(x, t) = 2.0 \cos\left[2\pi(10 t - 0.0080 x + 0.35)\right]\), where \(x\) and \(y\) are in centimetres and \(t\) is in seconds. What is the phase difference between two points on the wave separated by a distance of \(4.0\text{ m}\) at any fixed instant?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1:
Convert the separation distance into centimetres: \(\Delta x = 4.0\text{ m} = 400\text{ cm}\).

Step 2:
Identify the angular wave number \(k\) from the argument of the cosine function: \[k = 2\pi \times 0.0080\text{ rad cm}^{-1} = 0.016\pi\text{ rad cm}^{-1}\]

Step 3:
Calculate the phase difference at a fixed instant: \[\Delta\phi = k \Delta x = (0.016\pi\text{ rad cm}^{-1}) \times (400\text{ cm}) = 6.4\pi\text{ rad}\]

Step 4:
Evaluate numerically: \[\Delta\phi = 6.4 \times 3.14159\text{ rad} \approx 20.1\text{ rad}\]

Final Answer:
The phase difference between the two points is \(6.4\pi\text{ rad}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_NUMERICAL_Q07 - Phase difference for a particle over two milliseconds

questiontext.text: A sound wave of frequency \(250\text{ Hz}\) passes through a medium. What is the phase difference between the oscillations of a single particle of the medium at two instants separated by a time interval of \(2.0\text{ ms}\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1:
Identify the given frequency \(\nu = 250\text{ Hz}\) and time interval \(\Delta t = 2.0\text{ ms} = 2.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ s}\).

Step 2:
Calculate the angular frequency of oscillation: \[\omega = 2\pi \nu = 2\pi \times 250\text{ s}^{-1} = 500\pi\text{ rad s}^{-1}\]

Step 3:
Relate the phase difference of a single particle at a fixed position to the elapsed time interval: \[\Delta\phi = \omega \Delta t\]

Step 4:
Substitute the values: \[\Delta\phi = (500\pi\text{ rad s}^{-1}) \times (2.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ s}) = \pi\text{ rad}\]

Final Answer:
The phase difference is \(\pi\text{ rad}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_NUMERICAL_Q08 - Transverse wave speed calculation on steel wire under tension

questiontext.text: A steel wire \(0.72\text{ m}\) long has a total mass of \(5.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ kg}\). If the wire is subjected to a tensile force of \(60\text{ N}\), what is the speed of transverse waves propagating along the wire?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1:
Calculate the linear mass density \(\mu\) of the wire: \[\mu = \frac{\text{Mass}}{\text{Length}} = \frac{5.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ kg}}{0.72\text{ m}} \approx 6.944 \times 10^{-3}\text{ kg m}^{-1}\]

Step 2:
Recall the formula for the speed of a transverse wave on a stretched string: \[v = \sqrt{\frac{T}{\mu}}\]

Step 3:
Substitute the tension \(T = 60\text{ N}\) and linear mass density: \[v = \sqrt{\frac{60}{6.944 \times 10^{-3}}} = \sqrt{8640} \approx 93.0\text{ m s}^{-1}\]

Final Answer:
The speed of transverse waves on the wire is approximately \(93\text{ m s}^{-1}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_NUMERICAL_Q09 - Tension required for specified wave speed on string

questiontext.text: A stretched wire has a linear mass density of \(0.040\text{ kg m}^{-1}\). What tension must be applied to the wire to achieve a transverse wave speed of \(50\text{ m s}^{-1}\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1:
Given values: linear mass density \(\mu = 0.040\text{ kg m}^{-1}\) and wave speed \(v = 50\text{ m s}^{-1}\).

Step 2:
Write the formula for the speed of a transverse wave on a stretched string: \[v = \sqrt{\frac{T}{\mu}}\]

Step 3:
Rearrange to solve for the tension \(T\): \[T = \mu v^2\]

Step 4:
Substitute the given numbers: \[T = (0.040\text{ kg m}^{-1}) \times (50\text{ m s}^{-1})^2 = 0.040 \times 2500\text{ N} = 100\text{ N}\]

Final Answer:
The required tension is \(100\text{ N}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_NUMERICAL_Q10 - Transit time of transverse disturbance along stretched string

questiontext.text: A uniform string of mass \(2.50\text{ kg}\) and length \(20.0\text{ m}\) is stretched under a tension of \(200\text{ N}\). If a transverse jerk is struck at one end, how much time does the pulse take to reach the opposite end?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1:
Compute the linear mass density \(\mu\): \[\mu = \frac{2.50\text{ kg}}{20.0\text{ m}} = 0.125\text{ kg m}^{-1}\]

Step 2:
Compute the speed of the transverse wave: \[v = \sqrt{\frac{T}{\mu}} = \sqrt{\frac{200\text{ N}}{0.125\text{ kg m}^{-1}}} = \sqrt{1600} = 40.0\text{ m s}^{-1}\]

Step 3:
Calculate the time of travel over the length \(L = 20.0\text{ m}\): \[t = \frac{L}{v} = \frac{20.0\text{ m}}{40.0\text{ m s}^{-1}} = 0.50\text{ s}\]

Final Answer:
The time taken by the pulse to reach the other end is \(0.50\text{ s}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_NUMERICAL_Q11 - Wave speed ratio for two wires of different diameters

questiontext.text: Two wires A and B made of the same metal have diameters in the ratio \(1 : 3\). If both wires are stretched with the same tension, what is the ratio of the transverse wave speed in wire A to that in wire B?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1:
Express linear mass density in terms of material density \(\rho\) and diameter \(d\): \[\mu = \rho \frac{\pi d^2}{4}\]

Step 2:
Substitute \(\mu\) into the wave speed formula: \[v = \sqrt{\frac{T}{\mu}} = \sqrt{\frac{4T}{\rho \pi d^2}} = \frac{2}{d} \sqrt{\frac{T}{\pi \rho}}\]

Step 3:
Since \(T\) and \(\rho\) are identical for both wires, wave speed is inversely proportional to diameter: \[v \propto \frac{1}{d}\]

Step 4:
Calculate the ratio of speeds: \[\frac{v_A}{v_B} = \frac{d_B}{d_A} = \frac{3}{1}\]

Final Answer:
The ratio of wave speed in wire A to wire B is \(3 : 1\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_NUMERICAL_Q12 - Pulse transit time in vertically hanging heavy rope

questiontext.text: A uniform heavy rope of length \(L = 19.6\text{ m}\) and mass \(4.0\text{ kg}\) hangs vertically from a ceiling. Taking \(g = 9.8\text{ m s}^{-2}\), what is the time taken by a transverse wave pulse initiated at the bottom free end to reach the ceiling?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1:
At a height \(y\) above the bottom free end, the tension is equal to the weight of the rope segment below it: \[T(y) = \mu y g\]

Step 2:
The wave speed at height \(y\) is given by: \[v(y) = \sqrt{\frac{T(y)}{\mu}} = \sqrt{gy}\]

Step 3:
Express the differential transit time: \[dt = \frac{dy}{v(y)} = \frac{dy}{\sqrt{gy}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{g}} y^{-1/2} dy\]

Step 4:
Integrate from \(y = 0\) to \(y = L\): \[t = \frac{1}{\sqrt{g}} \left[ 2\sqrt{y} \right]_{0}^{L} = 2\sqrt{\frac{L}{g}}\]

Step 5:
Substitute \(L = 19.6\text{ m}\) and \(g = 9.8\text{ m s}^{-2}\): \[t = 2 \sqrt{\frac{19.6}{9.8}} = 2\sqrt{2} \approx 2 \times 1.414 = 2.83\text{ s}\]

Final Answer:
The time taken by the pulse to reach the ceiling is \(2.83\text{ s}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_NUMERICAL_Q13 - Tension required to equal sound speed in air

questiontext.text: A steel wire has a length of \(12.0\text{ m}\) and a mass of \(2.10\text{ kg}\). What tension must be applied to the wire so that the speed of transverse waves on it equals \(343\text{ m s}^{-1}\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1:
Compute the linear mass density \(\mu\): \[\mu = \frac{m}{L} = \frac{2.10\text{ kg}}{12.0\text{ m}} = 0.175\text{ kg m}^{-1}\]

Step 2:
Write the transverse wave speed formula for a string: \[v = \sqrt{\frac{T}{\mu}} \implies T = \mu v^2\]

Step 3:
Substitute \(\mu = 0.175\text{ kg m}^{-1}\) and \(v = 343\text{ m s}^{-1}\): \[T = 0.175 \times (343)^2 = 0.175 \times 117649 \approx 2.06 \times 10^4\text{ N}\]

Final Answer:
The required tension is \(2.06 \times 10^4\text{ N}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_NUMERICAL_Q14 - Bulk modulus calculation of water from sound speed

questiontext.text: In pure water at \(20^{\circ}\text{C}\), longitudinal sound waves propagate at a speed of \(1482\text{ m s}^{-1}\). Taking the density of water as \(1000\text{ kg m}^{-3}\), what is the bulk modulus of elasticity of water?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1:
Given data: speed of sound in fluid \(v = 1482\text{ m s}^{-1}\) and density \(\rho = 1000\text{ kg m}^{-3}\).

Step 2:
Write the formula for the speed of longitudinal waves in a fluid: \[v = \sqrt{\frac{B}{\rho}}\]

Step 3:
Rearrange to solve for the bulk modulus \(B\): \[B = \rho v^2\]

Step 4:
Substitute the numerical values: \[B = (1000\text{ kg m}^{-3}) \times (1482\text{ m s}^{-1})^2 = 1000 \times 2.1963 \times 10^6\text{ Pa} \approx 2.20 \times 10^9\text{ Pa}\]

Final Answer:
The bulk modulus of water is \(2.20 \times 10^9\text{ Pa}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_NUMERICAL_Q15 - Youngs modulus calculation for solid steel rod

questiontext.text: Longitudinal sound waves propagate along a solid steel rod at a speed of \(5000\text{ m s}^{-1}\). If the density of steel is \(7.8 \times 10^3\text{ kg m}^{-3}\), what is the Young's modulus of elasticity of the rod?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1:
Given: speed of longitudinal waves in solid rod \(v = 5000\text{ m s}^{-1}\) and density \(\rho = 7.8 \times 10^3\text{ kg m}^{-3}\).

Step 2:
Use the formula for longitudinal wave speed in a long solid bar: \[v = \sqrt{\frac{Y}{\rho}}\]

Step 3:
Solve for Young's modulus \(Y\): \[Y = \rho v^2\]

Step 4:
Substitute the values: \[Y = (7.8 \times 10^3\text{ kg m}^{-3}) \times (5000\text{ m s}^{-1})^2 = 7.8 \times 10^3 \times 2.5 \times 10^7\text{ Pa} = 1.95 \times 10^{11}\text{ Pa}\]

Final Answer:
The Young's modulus is \(1.95 \times 10^{11}\text{ Pa}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_NUMERICAL_Q16 - Percentage increase in sound speed by Laplace correction

questiontext.text: At standard temperature and pressure, the density of air is \(1.29\text{ kg m}^{-3}\) and atmospheric pressure is \(1.01 \times 10^5\text{ N m}^{-2}\). Newton's formula gives \(v_N = 280\text{ m s}^{-1}\), whereas Laplace's formula using \(\gamma = 1.40\) gives \(v_L = 331.3\text{ m s}^{-1}\). What is the percentage increase in the predicted speed of sound due to Laplace's correction?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1:
Identify the two speeds: Newton's isothermal speed \(v_N = 280\text{ m s}^{-1}\) and Laplace's adiabatic speed \(v_L = 331.3\text{ m s}^{-1}\).

Step 2:
Calculate the difference in speeds: \[\Delta v = v_L - v_N = 331.3 - 280 = 51.3\text{ m s}^{-1}\]

Step 3:
Compute the percentage increase relative to Newton's value: \[\text{Percentage Increase} = \\frac{\Delta v}{v_N} \times 100\% = \frac{51.3}{280} \times 100\% \approx 18.3\%\]

Final Answer:
The percentage increase is approximately \(18.3\%\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_NUMERICAL_Q17 - Speed of sound calculation at elevated temperature

questiontext.text: The speed of sound in air is \(332\text{ m s}^{-1}\) at \(0^{\circ}\text{C}\) (\(273\text{ K}\)). What is the speed of sound in air at \(27^{\circ}\text{C}\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1:
Convert temperatures to Kelvin: \(T_1 = 273\text{ K}\) and \(T_2 = 27 + 273 = 300\text{ K}\).

Step 2:
Recall that speed of sound in an ideal gas is directly proportional to the square root of absolute temperature: \[\frac{v_2}{v_1} = \sqrt{\frac{T_2}{T_1}}\]

Step 3:
Compute the temperature ratio: \[\sqrt{\frac{300}{273}} = \sqrt{1.0989} \approx 1.0483\]

Step 4:
Calculate the speed \(v_2\): \[v_2 = 332\text{ m s}^{-1} \times 1.0483 \approx 348\text{ m s}^{-1}\]

Final Answer:
The speed of sound at \(27^{\circ}\text{C}\) is \(348\text{ m s}^{-1}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_NUMERICAL_Q18 - Temperature required to triple the speed of sound

questiontext.text: At what temperature on the Celsius scale will the speed of sound in an ideal gas become three times its speed at \(0^{\circ}\text{C}\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1:
Let the speed at \(T_0 = 273\text{ K}\) be \(v_0\).

Step 2:
According to Laplace's formula, \(v \propto \sqrt{T}\).

Step 3:
For the speed to triple (\(v = 3 v_0\)): \[\frac{v}{v_0} = \sqrt{\frac{T}{T_0}} = 3 \implies \frac{T}{T_0} = 9\]

Step 4:
Calculate absolute temperature \(T\): \[T = 9 \times 273\text{ K} = 2457\text{ K}\]

Step 5:
Convert to degrees Celsius: \[t = T - 273 = 2457 - 273 = 2184^{\circ}\text{C}\]

Final Answer:
The temperature is \(2184^{\circ}\text{C}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_NUMERICAL_Q19 - Resultant amplitude of two waves in phase

questiontext.text: Two identical sinusoidal sound waves, each of amplitude \(4.0\text{ mm}\), arrive at a microphone with zero phase difference. What is the amplitude of the resultant sound wave detected by the microphone?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1:
Given amplitudes \(a_1 = a_2 = a = 4.0\text{ mm}\) and phase difference \(\phi = 0\).

Step 2:
Recall the resultant amplitude formula for two interfering harmonic waves: \[A = 2a \cos\left(\frac{\phi}{2}\right)\]

Step 3:
Substitute \(\phi = 0\): \[A = 2(4.0\text{ mm}) \cos(0) = 8.0\text{ mm}\]

Step 4:
This corresponds to completely constructive interference.

Final Answer:
The resultant amplitude is \(8.0\text{ mm}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_NUMERICAL_Q20 - Resultant amplitude for phase difference of two pi over three

questiontext.text: Two coherent harmonic waves of equal amplitude \(a = 6.0\text{ cm}\) superpose at a point with a phase difference of \(\phi = \frac{2\pi}{3}\text{ rad}\). What is the amplitude of the resulting wave?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1:
Given equal amplitudes \(a = 6.0\text{ cm}\) and phase difference \(\phi = \frac{2\pi}{3}\text{ rad}\).

Step 2:
Write the formula for resultant amplitude: \[A = 2a \cos\left(\frac{\phi}{2}\right)\]

Step 3:
Evaluate half the phase angle: \[\frac{\phi}{2} = \frac{1}{2} \left(\frac{2\pi}{3}\right) = \frac{\pi}{3}\text{ rad} = 60^{\circ}\]

Step 4:
Calculate \(\cos(60^{\circ}) = 0.5\).

Step 5:
Compute resultant amplitude: \[A = 2 \times 6.0\text{ cm} \times 0.5 = 6.0\text{ cm}\]

Final Answer:
The resultant amplitude is \(6.0\text{ cm}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_NUMERICAL_Q21 - Ratio of maximum to minimum intensity in interference

questiontext.text: Two coherent wave sources produce vibrations of amplitudes \(5.0\text{ units}\) and \(3.0\text{ units}\). What is the ratio of maximum to minimum intensity in the interference pattern?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1:
Given amplitudes: \(a_1 = 5.0\) and \(a_2 = 3.0\).

Step 2:
Maximum amplitude occurs during constructive interference: \[A_{\text{max}} = a_1 + a_2 = 5.0 + 3.0 = 8.0\]

Step 3:
Minimum amplitude occurs during destructive interference: \[A_{\text{min}} = a_1 - a_2 = 5.0 - 3.0 = 2.0\]

Step 4:
Since intensity is proportional to amplitude squared: \[\frac{I_{\text{max}}}{I_{\text{min}}} = \left(\frac{A_{\text{max}}}{A_{\text{min}}}\right)^2 = \left(\frac{8.0}{2.0}\right)^2 = (4)^2 = \frac{16}{1}\]

Final Answer:
The ratio of maximum to minimum intensity is \(16 : 1\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_NUMERICAL_Q22 - Amplitude ratio deduction from intensity ratio twenty five to one

questiontext.text: In an interference experiment between two coherent sound waves, the ratio of maximum intensity to minimum intensity is \(25 : 1\). What is the ratio of the amplitudes \(\frac{a_1}{a_2}\) of the two interfering waves?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1:
Relate intensity ratio to amplitude ratio: \[\frac{I_{\text{max}}}{I_{\text{min}}} = \left(\frac{a_1 + a_2}{a_1 - a_2}\right)^2 = 25\]

Step 2:
Take the square root on both sides: \[\frac{a_1 + a_2}{a_1 - a_2} = 5\]

Step 3:
Cross-multiply: \[a_1 + a_2 = 5(a_1 - a_2) = 5a_1 - 5a_2\]

Step 4:
Rearrange terms: \[6a_2 = 4a_1 \implies \frac{a_1}{a_2} = \frac{6}{4} = \frac{3}{2} = 1.5\]

Final Answer:
The ratio of amplitudes is \(3 : 2\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_NUMERICAL_Q23 - Oscillation amplitude calculation in stationary wave at distance

questiontext.text: A stationary wave on a string fixed at both ends is described by \(y(x, t) = 0.06 \sin\left(\frac{2\pi}{3} x\right) \cos(120\pi t)\), where \(x\) and \(y\) are in metres and \(t\) in seconds. What is the amplitude of oscillation of a point located at \(x = 0.375\text{ m}\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1:
The amplitude of oscillation at position \(x\) in this stationary wave is given by: \[A(x) = 0.06 \left| \sin\left(\frac{2\pi}{3} x\right) \right|\]

Step 2:
Substitute \(x = 0.375\text{ m} = \frac{3}{8}\text{ m}\): \[\frac{2\pi}{3} \times \frac{3}{8} = \frac{2\pi}{8} = \frac{\pi}{4}\text{ rad}\]

Step 3:
Calculate \(\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \approx 0.7071\).

Step 4:
Compute the amplitude: \[A = 0.06\text{ m} \times 0.7071 \approx 0.0424\text{ m} = 4.24\text{ cm}\]

Final Answer:
The amplitude of oscillation is \(4.24\text{ cm}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_NUMERICAL_Q24 - Wavelength and speed of component waves in standing wave

questiontext.text: The transverse displacement of a string is given by \(y(x, t) = 0.06 \sin\left(\frac{2\pi}{3} x\right) \cos(120\pi t)\), where \(x, y\) are in metres and \(t\) in seconds. Interpreting this as the superposition of two identical waves travelling in opposite directions, what are the wavelength \(\lambda\) and speed \(v\) of each component wave?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1:
Use the trigonometric identity \(2 \sin A \cos B = \sin(A - B) + \sin(A + B)\).

Step 2:
Here, \(y(x, t) = 0.03 \sin\left(\frac{2\pi}{3} x - 120\pi t\right) + 0.03 \sin\left(\frac{2\pi}{3} x + 120\pi t\right)\).

Step 3:
Extract wave number \(k = \frac{2\pi}{3}\text{ rad m}^{-1}\) and angular frequency \(\omega = 120\pi\text{ rad s}^{-1}\).

Step 4:
Calculate the wavelength: \[\lambda = \frac{2\pi}{k} = \frac{2\pi}{\frac{2\pi}{3}} = 3.0\text{ m}\]

Step 5:
Calculate the frequency: \[\nu = \frac{\omega}{2\pi} = \frac{120\pi}{2\pi} = 60\text{ Hz}\]

Step 6:
Calculate the wave speed: \[v = \frac{\omega}{k} = \lambda \nu = 3.0\text{ m} \times 60\text{ s}^{-1} = 180\text{ m s}^{-1}\]

Final Answer:
Each component wave has wavelength \(3.0\text{ m}\) and speed \(180\text{ m s}^{-1}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_NUMERICAL_Q25 - Tension calculation in vibrating clamped string

questiontext.text: A string clamped at both ends has length \(1.5\text{ m}\) and mass \(3.0 \times 10^{-2}\text{ kg}\). If transverse waves propagate along the string at a speed of \(180\text{ m s}^{-1}\), what is the tension in the string?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1:
Compute the linear mass density \(\mu\) of the string: \[\mu = \frac{\text{Mass}}{\text{Length}} = \frac{3.0 \times 10^{-2}\text{ kg}}{1.5\text{ m}} = 2.0 \times 10^{-2}\text{ kg m}^{-1}\]

Step 2:
Use the transverse wave speed formula for a stretched string: \[v = \sqrt{\frac{T}{\mu}} \implies T = \mu v^2\]

Step 3:
Substitute the given values: \[T = (2.0 \times 10^{-2}\text{ kg m}^{-1}) \times (180\text{ m s}^{-1})^2 = 0.020 \times 32400\text{ N} = 648\text{ N}\]

Final Answer:
The tension in the string is \(648\text{ N}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_NUMERICAL_Q26 - Wave speed on string vibrating in fundamental mode

questiontext.text: A wire stretched between two rigid supports vibrates in its fundamental mode with a frequency of \(45\text{ Hz}\). The mass of the wire is \(3.5 \times 10^{-2}\text{ kg}\) and its linear mass density is \(4.0 \times 10^{-2}\text{ kg m}^{-1}\). What is the speed of a transverse wave on the wire?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1:
Calculate the length \(L\) of the stretched wire: \[L = \frac{\text{Mass}}{\mu} = \frac{3.5 \times 10^{-2}\text{ kg}}{4.0 \times 10^{-2}\text{ kg m}^{-1}} = 0.875\text{ m}\]

Step 2:
For a wire fixed at both ends vibrating in its fundamental mode: \[\lambda = 2L = 2 \times 0.875\text{ m} = 1.75\text{ m}\]

Step 3:
Calculate the wave speed using \(v = \nu \lambda\): \[v = 45\text{ s}^{-1} \times 1.75\text{ m} = 78.75\text{ m s}^{-1} \approx 79\text{ m s}^{-1}\]

Final Answer:
The wave speed is approximately \(79\text{ m s}^{-1}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_NUMERICAL_Q27 - Tension in wire vibrating at fundamental frequency

questiontext.text: A wire having a linear mass density of \(4.0 \times 10^{-2}\text{ kg m}^{-1}\) vibrates in its fundamental mode with a frequency of \(45\text{ Hz}\). If the speed of the transverse wave on the wire is \(78.75\text{ m s}^{-1}\), what is the tension in the wire?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1:
Given: linear mass density \(\mu = 4.0 \times 10^{-2}\text{ kg m}^{-1}\) and wave speed \(v = 78.75\text{ m s}^{-1}\).

Step 2:
Use the relationship between tension, wave speed, and linear mass density: \[T = \mu v^2\]

Step 3:
Substitute the values: \[T = (4.0 \times 10^{-2}\text{ kg m}^{-1}) \times (78.75\text{ m s}^{-1})^2 = 0.040 \times 6201.56\text{ N} \approx 248\text{ N}\]

Final Answer:
The tension in the wire is approximately \(248\text{ N}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_NUMERICAL_Q28 - Fundamental frequency under simultaneous length and tension change

questiontext.text: A sonometer wire of length \(0.50\text{ m}\) vibrates in its fundamental mode with a frequency of \(250\text{ Hz}\) under a tension of \(100\text{ N}\). If the length of the wire is increased to \(0.60\text{ m}\) and the tension is increased to \(144\text{ N}\), what is the new fundamental frequency?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1:
Write the formula for the fundamental frequency of a stretched wire: \[ u = rac{1}{2L} \sqrt{ rac{T}{\mu}}\]

Step 2:
Since the wire material and linear mass density \(\mu\) remain constant: \[ rac{ u_2}{ u_1} = rac{L_1}{L_2} \sqrt{ rac{T_2}{T_1}}\]

Step 3:
Substitute the given values \(L_1 = 0.50 ext{ m}\), \(L_2 = 0.60 ext{ m}\), \(T_1 = 100 ext{ N}\), and \(T_2 = 144 ext{ N}\): \[ rac{ u_2}{250} = rac{0.50}{0.60} \sqrt{ rac{144}{100}} = rac{5}{6} imes rac{12}{10} = rac{5}{6} imes rac{6}{5} = 1\]

Step 4:
Compute the new frequency: \[ u_2 = 250 ext{ Hz}\]

Final Answer:
The new fundamental frequency remains \(250 ext{ Hz}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_NUMERICAL_Q29 - Resonating harmonic mode of open organ pipe

questiontext.text: A pipe \(30.0\text{ cm}\) long is open at both ends. Taking the speed of sound in air as \(330\text{ m s}^{-1}\), which harmonic mode of the pipe resonates with an acoustic source of frequency \(1.10\text{ kHz}\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1:
Convert pipe length to metres: \(L = 30.0 ext{ cm} = 0.300 ext{ m}\).

Step 2:
Compute the fundamental frequency of the open pipe: \[ u_1 = rac{v}{2L} = rac{330 ext{ m s}^{-1}}{2 imes 0.300 ext{ m}} = rac{330}{0.600} = 550 ext{ Hz}\]

Step 3:
The frequencies of the harmonic modes are integer multiples: \( u_n = n u_1\).

Step 4:
Determine the harmonic number \(n\) for \( u = 1.10 ext{ kHz} = 1100 ext{ Hz}\): \[n = rac{ u}{ u_1} = rac{1100 ext{ Hz}}{550 ext{ Hz}} = 2\]

Step 5:
Thus, the pipe resonates in its second harmonic mode.

Final Answer:
The pipe resonates in its second harmonic mode.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_NUMERICAL_Q30 - Fundamental resonance of closed organ pipe

questiontext.text: A pipe \(20.0\text{ cm}\) long is closed at one end and open at the other. If the speed of sound in air is \(340\text{ m s}^{-1}\), what is the fundamental resonant frequency of the pipe?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1:
Convert pipe length to metres: \(L = 20.0\text{ cm} = 0.200\text{ m}\).

Step 2:
Recall the fundamental frequency formula for a pipe closed at one end: \[\nu_1 = \frac{v}{4L}\]

Step 3:
Substitute \(v = 340\text{ m s}^{-1}\) and \(L = 0.200\text{ m}\): \[\nu_1 = \frac{340\text{ m s}^{-1}}{4 \times 0.200\text{ m}} = \frac{340}{0.800} = 425\text{ Hz}\]

Final Answer:
The fundamental resonant frequency is \(425\text{ Hz}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_NUMERICAL_Q31 - Length ratio of open to closed organ pipes

questiontext.text: An open organ pipe and a closed organ pipe have identical fundamental frequencies. What is the ratio of the length of the open pipe to the length of the closed pipe?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1:
Write the fundamental frequency formula for an open pipe of length \(L_o\): \[\nu_{\text{open}} = \frac{v}{2L_o}\]

Step 2:
Write the fundamental frequency formula for a closed pipe of length \(L_c\): \[\nu_{\text{closed}} = \frac{v}{4L_c}\]

Step 3:
Equate the two frequencies: \[\frac{v}{2L_o} = \frac{v}{4L_c}\]

Step 4:
Solve for the ratio \(\frac{L_o}{L_c}\): \[\frac{1}{2L_o} = \frac{1}{4L_c} \implies 4L_c = 2L_o \implies \frac{L_o}{L_c} = \frac{4}{2} = 2 : 1\]

Final Answer:
The ratio of the length of the open pipe to the closed pipe is \(2 : 1\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_NUMERICAL_Q32 - Sound speed and end correction in resonance tube

questiontext.text: In a resonance tube experiment using a tuning fork of frequency \(512\text{ Hz}\), the first resonance occurs at an air column length of \(16.0\text{ cm}\) and the second resonance occurs at \(49.0\text{ cm}\). What are the speed of sound in air and the end correction of the tube?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1:
Given: frequency \(\nu = 512\text{ Hz}\), first resonance length \(l_1 = 16.0\text{ cm} = 0.160\text{ m}\), second resonance length \(l_2 = 49.0\text{ cm} = 0.490\text{ m}\).

Step 2:
The separation between successive resonances in a closed tube is half a wavelength: \[l_2 - l_1 = \frac{\lambda}{2} \implies \lambda = 2(l_2 - l_1)\]

Step 3:
Calculate \(\lambda\): \[\lambda = 2(0.490\text{ m} - 0.160\text{ m}) = 2(0.330\text{ m}) = 0.660\text{ m}\]

Step 4:
Calculate the speed of sound: \[v = \nu \lambda = 512\text{ s}^{-1} \times 0.660\text{ m} \approx 338\text{ m s}^{-1}\]

Step 5:
Calculate the end correction \(e\) using \(l_1 + e = \frac{\lambda}{4}\): \[e = \frac{\lambda}{4} - l_1 = \frac{66.0\text{ cm}}{4} - 16.0\text{ cm} = 16.5\text{ cm} - 16.0\text{ cm} = 0.5\text{ cm}\]

Final Answer:
The speed of sound is \(338\text{ m s}^{-1}\) and the end correction is \(0.5\text{ cm}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_NUMERICAL_Q33 - Speed of sound in steel rod clamped at midpoint

questiontext.text: A steel rod \(100\text{ cm}\) long is clamped rigidly at its center. The fundamental frequency of longitudinal vibrations is found to be \(2.53\text{ kHz}\). What is the speed of sound in steel?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1:
Given: length \(L = 100\text{ cm} = 1.00\text{ m}\) and fundamental frequency \(\nu = 2.53\text{ kHz} = 2530\text{ Hz}\).

Step 2:
For a rod clamped at its center, the center is a displacement node and both free ends are displacement antinodes.

Step 3:
In the fundamental mode, the rod contains half a wavelength: \[L = \frac{\lambda}{2} \implies \lambda = 2L = 2(1.00\text{ m}) = 2.00\text{ m}\]

Step 4:
Calculate the speed of sound: \[v = \nu \lambda = 2530\text{ s}^{-1} \times 2.00\text{ m} = 5060\text{ m s}^{-1}\]

Final Answer:
The speed of sound in steel is \(5060\text{ m s}^{-1}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_WAVES_NUMERICAL_Q34 - Time elapsed before splash of stone is heard

questiontext.text: A stone is dropped from the top of a tower of height \(300\text{ m}\) into a pond below. Given \(g = 9.8\text{ m s}^{-2}\) and the speed of sound in air is \(340\text{ m s}^{-1}\), how many seconds after release is the sound of the splash heard at the top?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1:
